title: Barre VT Insulation Rebates 2026: Up to $3,000 and Old-House Basics
desc: Barre insulation and air sealing rebates for 2026: Efficiency Vermont pays 75% up to $3,000, or up to $7,000 if income-eligible, for a city where 46% of homes were built before 1940 and half rent.
lead: Nearly half of Barre's homes (46%) were built before 1940, 58% burn oil, and half of households rent. Efficiency Vermont's insulation rebate fits that mix, if the owner and the person paying the bill can agree.
cards_heading: What pays for insulation and air sealing in Barre
cards_intro: We re-read Efficiency Vermont's Home Performance with ENERGY STAR page and its list of related offers on October 5, 2026. Barre is Green Mountain Power electricity territory, and Efficiency Vermont runs the weatherization offer for customers of utilities other than Burlington Electric and Vermont Gas.

cards.title: Efficiency Vermont weatherization
cards.note: 75% of a qualifying insulation and air-sealing project, up to $3,000, while funding lasts (effective July 1, 2026). The project needs an Efficiency Excellence Network contractor and at least a 10% cut in air leakage on the blower-door test.

cards.title: Income-eligible weatherization
cards.note: For low- and moderate-income households whose property is their primary residence. Efficiency Vermont also lists a free Weatherization Assistance Program through a partner for income-qualified homes.

cards.title: Do-it-yourself weatherization
cards.note: Efficiency Vermont lists $100 for DIY weatherization. Burlington Electric describes it as completing at least three do-it-yourself projects. Good for weatherstripping, door sweeps and attic hatches.

cards.title: Weatherization financing
cards.note: Through Vermont Gas, Green Mountain Credit Union lends up to $20,000 over five years at 0% for weatherization. The Weatherization Repayment Assistance Program (WRAP) puts repayment on the utility bill instead.

after_cards: The same offer applies in all four Green Mountain Power cities we cover. What changes is the building you are insulating.
sections: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey counts 4,335 housing units in Barre. 2,012 were built in 1939 or earlier (46%), 472 in the 1940s and 1950s, 846 in the 1960s and 1970s, 662 in the 1980s and 1990s and 343 since 2000. That is the second-oldest housing profile of the five cities, behind Rutland. Of 4,094 occupied homes, 2,385 use fuel oil as the main fuel.

2,062 Barre households own and 2,032 rent. 1,922 housing units are in buildings of two to nine units. Insulation is the classic split-incentive problem: the landlord pays and the tenant saves on heat, unless the tenant pays the heat bill and the landlord does nothing. Efficiency Vermont's Home Performance offer covers existing one-to-four-unit homes, which describes most of Barre's small rental buildings, although we did not confirm whether it accepts rental owners.

A practical arrangement is for the landlord to apply for the rebate and the tenant to agree to stay through a winter, so both can see the effect on the heating bill.

75% of qualifying insulation and air-sealing cost up to $3,000, or up to $7,000 for low- and moderate-income households in a primary residence (effective July 1, 2026, while funding lasts). It needs an Efficiency Excellence Network contractor and at least a 10% air-leakage reduction. Efficiency Vermont also lists $100 for DIY weatherization, a free Virtual Home Energy Visit and free services for income-qualified Vermonters.

Barre's average January low is -11.9°C and its coldest recorded day between 2015 and 2024 was -30.9°C. An oil boiler in a leaky house burns the most when the weather is coldest. Cutting the load first means a smaller boiler or heat pump will do the job, and it makes any later heat pump cheaper. See our Barre heat pump guide.

Barre and Montpelier share the same Green Mountain Power and Efficiency Vermont offers, so the rebate is identical. The difference is the housing: Barre has more oil, more pre-1940 buildings and an even owner and renter split. See the Montpelier insulation guide for the neighbouring city.
claim_heading: How to claim an insulation rebate in Barre
claim_steps: Book Efficiency Vermont's free Virtual Home Energy Visit, or ask a contractor for a blower-door test.
Choose an Efficiency Excellence Network contractor, since the rebate requires one.
Plan air sealing first, then insulation, and agree the target air-leakage cut (at least 10%) in writing.
If your income may qualify, ask Efficiency Vermont about the $7,000 tier before the work starts.
Keep the before-and-after test results with your invoice.
faq: What does Efficiency Vermont pay for insulation in Barre?
75% of a qualifying project up to $3,000, or up to $7,000 for low- and moderate-income households in their primary residence.
Can a Barre landlord claim the rebate?
Efficiency Vermont's offer covers existing one-to-four-unit homes. We did not confirm a rental option, and the $7,000 tier is for a primary residence, so ask Efficiency Vermont.
A contractor in Efficiency Vermont's Efficiency Excellence Network. The project must cut air leakage by at least 10%.
Is there a free option for low-income households?
Efficiency Vermont lists a free Weatherization Assistance Program through a partner and free services for income-qualified Vermonters. We did not read the income limits.
Ask the landlord about the program, report drafts in writing, and do small DIY jobs. Efficiency Vermont lists $100 for DIY weatherization.
